source.paraphrase: A saga owner must register and validate the complete graph before start. Node identities and expected or previous step references must have one owner and an explicit meaning. Use of the deprecated structured-saga API must have a recorded version and replacement decision.

invariants.why: A saga owner must register and validate the complete graph before start. Node identities and expected or previous step references must have one owner and an explicit meaning. Use of the deprecated structured-saga API must have a recorded version and replacement decision. The product uses DStructuredSaga or its public node and event-builder contracts. This pack must not force new adoption of a deprecated API.
invariants.fixHint: Exercise the actual registered graph, including duplicate or missing references and registration after start. The pinned runtime validates join references to steps but does not validate previousStepId or wire nodes added while running. Joins cannot name another join as an expected step. Review the declaration's deprecation and the product's supported-version decision. source.paraphrase: A saga boundary must validate authorization, organization scope, event identity and payload before admission. A matching sagaId must not be treated as authorization or proof that an internal step ran. Data shared with queued handlers must have explicit mutation ownership.

invariants.why: A saga boundary must validate authorization, organization scope, event identity and payload before admission. source.paraphrase: A saga handler must complete its owned asynchronous work and return the declared outcome. It must use literal failure for an expected failed step, or an observed exception for an unexpected failure. Repeated delivery must not repeat an unsafe business effect.

invariants.why: A saga handler must complete its owned asynchronous work and return the declared outcome. It must use literal failure for an expected failed step, or an observed exception for an unexpected failure. Repeated delivery must not repeat an unsafe business effect. A registered structured-saga step performs a decision or effect.

Void means success in the pinned API; false and unknown values are also runtime successes and must not be used as failure signals. In-memory duplicate suppression ends when stop resets state. source.paraphrase: Each compensating effect must have an explicit failure, retry and idempotency policy. A checkpoint must define which successful effects are retained and which failed effects still need compensation. Compensation must not be assumed to be an atomic rollback.

invariants.why: Each compensating effect must have an explicit failure, retry and idempotency policy. A checkpoint must define which successful effects are retained and which failed effects still need compensation. Compensation must not be assumed to be an atomic rollback. The graph has compensate, previousStepId or isCheckpoint behavior, or a join can compensate a completed branch.
invariants.fixHint: Verify actual own-before-previous ordering, failure propagation and repeat safety. A succeeded checkpoint blocks a later compensation request, but a failed checkpoint still runs its own compensation. Reject a compensation promise and verify the owner's recovery policy: the pinned runtime can retain running state, remove the queued event and ignore later input without raising branch failure. source.paraphrase: A saga join must use trusted completion signals and a verified any or every branch policy. Winning, losing, failing and already completed branches must have explicit business outcomes. A join signal alone must not prove that its expected handlers ran.

invariants.why: A saga join must use trusted completion signals and a verified any or every branch policy. Winning, losing, failing and already completed branches must have explicit business outcomes. A join signal alone must not prove that its expected handlers ran. The graph registers a join or consumes structured-saga success, branch-failure or cancellation events.
invariants.fixHint: Exercise distinct successes, duplicate or forged success, one or all failed branches, already succeeded losers and same-branch siblings. The pinned any join cancels a different idle branch but does not cancel an idle sibling in the winner's branch; an already succeeded loser can be compensated. Every failure cancels branches and requests compensation for recorded successes. Verify actual application effects and failure outputs, not only counter equality. source.paraphrase: A saga's durable-work and replay contract must verify actual storage selection, recovery, acknowledgement and business-effect idempotency. A configured persistence singleton or in-memory step state must not stand in for durable execution state.

invariants.why: A saga's durable-work and replay contract must verify actual storage selection, recovery, acknowledgement and business-effect idempotency. A configured persistence singleton or in-memory step state must not stand in for durable execution state. A saga must survive process loss, resume effects or share a queue identity across instances. A deliberately volatile custom queue needs an explicit loss policy.

The pinned saga admits a built-in queue when a persistence singleton exists, but that queue's transient fallback does not select the singleton repository.
